recommendation.summary: dsh-tui 0.11.1 is an interactive terminal UI plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Its own README declares the TUI surface and the exact installation profile dsh-tui (`dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`), so executionProfiles is tui with tuiProfile dsh-tui; no author Web, headless, SDK or ACP workflow is claimed (the web-coexistence script only checks that the TUI patch yields to an official web-app row). Node intent: engines.node is `^22.19 || >=24` in both source and published manifests (declared support for 22 and 24), and the README states CI uses Node 24 with pnpm 11, corroborated by node-version: 24 in .github/workflows/ci.yml; no author-recommended major is stated, so preferredNodeMajor is the CI-configured 24. packageManager is pnpm@11.21.0 (development scope). The author's primary validated DSH line is 0.1.7-rc.2 (README primary compatibility target plus the pnpm-workspace.yaml dev-tree pin comment), which is older than the Radar host 0.2.0-rc.1 and is not covered by the published peer ranges; that mismatch is recorded as a coverage gap, not as compatibility.

conclusion.statement: dsh-tui 0.11.1 (@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui) was reviewed and exercised on the author's primary validated DSH line 0.1.7-rc.2 and on the Radar host 0.2.0-rc.1, on Node 22 and Node 24. Author intent: the plugin's own README declares an interactive terminal UI and the exact installation profile dsh-tui (`dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`), so executionProfiles is tui with tuiProfile dsh-tui; no author Web, headless, SDK or ACP workflow is claimed. Node intent: engines.node `^22.19 || >=24` in both source and published manifests (declared support for 22 and 24) and CI-configured Node 24 (README 'CI uses Node 24 and pnpm 11', .github/workflows/ci.yml node-version: 24); no author-recommended major is stated, so preferredNodeMajor is the CI-configured 24. packageManager pnpm@11.21.0 is development scope. Results: on DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 the exact artifact installed, registered, loaded and satisfied its direct Node peer contracts on both Node 22 and Node 24 (native result compatible), and the TUI surface produced a real PTY frame, accepted input and completed controlled shutdown on both majors (surface result compatible, all stages passed). On the Radar host DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 both native cells are unknown: the plugin install did not produce a bounded command result and the install phase hit its 180s timeout on both Node 22 and Node 24, so no compatibility claim is made for 0.2.0-rc.1. The 0.2.0-rc.1 host is outside the plugin's published peer ranges (which end at 0.1.7-rc.2), consistent with the author's stated primary target. No adapter (SDK/ACP) cell was scheduled, and no authenticated integration was exercised.
coverageNotes: DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 (the Radar host) is unproven: both native cells returned unknown because the plugin install produced no bounded command result and timed out at 180s on Node 22 and Node 24; the published peer ranges end at 0.1.7-rc.2.
Author DSH baseline 0.1.7-rc.2 differs from the Radar host 0.2.0-rc.1; the compatible results above are for the author baseline only and do not transfer to 0.2.0-rc.1.
No SDK or ACP adapter cell was scheduled (adapterCells 0); the plugin claims no SDK/ACP workflow, so those planes are untested.
Authenticated integrations were not exercised and cannot be completed by Radar: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, /login, and subscription OAuth via the bundled dsh-auth dependency.

Interactive TUI coverage is limited to PTY frame, input acceptance and controlled shutdown; rendering fidelity, mouse/selection, image protocols (Kitty/Sixel), Mermaid/LaTeX rendering and long-session behaviour were not verified.

pnpm-workspace.yaml dev-tree overrides pin the @deepseek-ai tree to 0.1.7-rc.2 for the development fixture tree only and are never consulted by consumer installs; its parent>child selectors (@dsh-tui-dev/sqlite-island>@deepseek-ai/dsh-*) are unsupported selectors and were not transferred to any profile.
pnpm >=11 install-script blocking (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS) and the foreign-platform @img/sharp-* skip are documented install-time prerequisites that Radar did not reproduce.

docs/getting-started.md, docs/getting-started.en.md, docs/README.md, docs/configuration.md and docs/configuration.en.md were omitted by the evidence byte budget; Radar retains an incomplete-collection coverage flag.
The plugin's own README documents a Windows profile default of danger-full-access with approval never; that security posture was not exercised or evaluated.
